Interface Multimap<K,V>

Type Parameters:
K - the key type
V - the value type
All Known Subinterfaces:
ListMultimap<K,V>, SetMultimap<K,V>
All Known Implementing Classes:
HashListMultimap, HashSetMultimap
public interface Multimap<K,V>
A collection that maps keys to values, like a Map, but where a key may have several values: its entries are key-value pairs, and a key is in the multimap as long as it has a value. 
ListMultimap<String, Integer> scores = HashListMultimap.create();
scores.put("alice", 3);
scores.put("alice", 5);
scores.put("bob", 4);
scores.get("alice"); // [3, 5]
scores.size();       // 3

A ListMultimap keeps the values of a key in a list, in the order they were added, duplicates included. A SetMultimap keeps them in a set, without duplicates.

Its views are live: get(Object), keySet(), values(), entries() and asMap() reflect the changes made to the multimap, and removing from them removes from the multimap. Only get(key) supports adding. A key whose last value is removed, through the multimap or a view, leaves the multimap.

size() is the number of entries, up to Integer.MAX_VALUE. No multimap of this library contains null keys or values.

Since:
0.1.2

      Returns a live view of the values of all keys, each value as many times as it occurs, grouped by key.

      the values of this multimap

      the entries of this multimap

      Returns:
      this multimap as a map

    • equals

      boolean equals(@Nullable Object o)
      Returns whether another object is a multimap with the same keys and values. Two multimaps are equal when their asMap() views are, so a ListMultimap equals another one with the same values in the same order, and a SetMultimap another one with the same values in any order. A list multimap never equals a set multimap, unless both are empty.
      Overrides:
      equals in class Object
      Parameters:
      o - the object to compare with
      Returns:
      true if o is an equal multimap
